svg.text: Up to sixteen reflective IR channels on a shared pulsed LED bus, multiplexed onto two analog inputs.
WARNING: in variant A, never have one board live while the other is dark.
TO-220 from the front: G, D, S
Installed in the machine: own regulator on the board, fed with 5 V through J-PWR.
keep together: 100 nF adjacent to U1 pins 2/3, C1 and C3 as short as possible
VARIANT B: supplied from the Teensy (prototype / breadboard)
Supplied from the Teensy’s 3V3 pin, no regulator. The channel section above is unchanged.
At the 3.3 V entry, leads short.
Budget: 179 mA worst case at sixteen channels,
No fault isolation: a short on the
sensor cable hits the regulator inside the Teensy.
B ends when A is built: populate U1, its capacitors
and J-PWR, move the 3.3 V feed, re-terminate J-T.
C5 and C6 are variant B only. C5 on variant A’s rail,
powering up with the LED bus on, would demand 313 mA.
MCP1700 pin order: 1 = GND, 2 = IN, 3 = OUT, not the 7805 or LD1117 order.
C2 at U1 pin 2, C4 at U1 pin 3
shortest path for the high-frequency current
C1 at U1 pin 2, C3 at U1 pin 3
output capacitor is in the LDO control loop
1 kΩ gate resistor, 100 kΩ pull-down at Q1 gate
gate loop pickup, defined gate at boot
C5 and C6 at the 3.3 V entry, variant B
filters what arrives, where it arrives
The MCP1700 datasheet states no placement distance, so none is claimed here. What matters is which parts belong together, listed above.
